description:
Policy page: https://claude.ai/artifact/8LRFmBY6vNCuTw1dmANBnE (when fz specializes a function; measured at develop f822f0f84).

Symptom that opened this: Kernel.panic/1 and fz_panic/1 get one activation per exception type raised (12 activations, about 115 jobs on the distiller). The old proposal here (merge maps at Ignore positions of non-recursive bodies) misread the trigger and is withdrawn.

The trigger, measured:
A. A non-recursive body keys every Ignore position by its verbatim structure (KeyCollapse::Literals); only a recursive body takes the demand-driven convergence collapse (KeyCollapse::Structure). panic/1's argument is asked nothing and not returned, so each exception struct is its own key.
B. A record's convergence class keeps every field (convergence_class / convergence_class_at), so even the Structure collapse keys two structs apart at a position nothing asks about. No reason is recorded.
Specs play no part: a @spec narrows only open (var-carrying) arguments. The root axis duplicates nothing (0 cross-root pairs on the distiller, 00420, the raise probe).

Experiments (local switches, never committed):
- A, Structure for every body: 107 fixture failures. The callable part of the non-recursive verbatim rule is load-bearing (reducer lambdas sharing a key, 00773 smallest); the root cause is filed as fz-lr6.
- C, Structure for every body with callables kept: every fixture passes; distiller 12,892 -> 12,868 jobs; pins: 00567 executables 79 -> 77, stream activations 140 -> 138, native body walks 175 -> 172, aggregate 1325 -> 1320 fall; 00420 mutually-subtype ids 122 -> 142 and product_drive list pairs 6 -> 7 rise; callable_target exact key id moves.
- C+B (maps at an unasked position collapse): same as C plus 00420 static-reach and Recursive pins; distiller 12,884 jobs; panic/1 and the sink/pass probes merge.

Target policy: a key names what the callee's demand names (what a dispatch reads, the literals a question tells apart, the positions the return is built from, callable identity where it is returned or consumed); every other position is its convergence class, recursive or not. The Structure/Literals split goes.

Open before code, each answered by an experiment:
1. Where the 00420 mutually-subtype id rise (122 -> 142) and the product_drive extra list pair (6 -> 7) under C come from. A rise is explained or refuted before anything lands.
2. What a record's class is at an unasked position (keep __struct__ and drop fields, or the map class), and whether two structs merged under one key change their runtime lane (value_lane_repr types maps exactly); checked against the transport code and a native run.
3. Whether Recursive keeps readers once keying no longer reads it.
4. A protocol callback's returned axis per receiver type (below), measured against fz-lr6's +510 before it lands.
Also folded: the 'keys as itself, else wait on Recursive and InputDemand' test exists three times (World::require_activation_key_facts, backend.rs, callable_target.rs) and becomes one World method.

Folded from fz-l3p (closed): a protocol callback's returned axis.
keying.rs visit_protocol_callback marks every non-receiver input of a callback returned Whole, so under fz-lr6 Enumerable.reduce_while/3's reducer keeps its brand in every Enum wrapper's key. Suite census (849 fixtures, applied work, interp, measured at a18fb1519):
- base 364,735; fz-lr6 alone +510 (18 fixtures up; 00420 +124, 01129 +209, 00571 +77). This +510 is the most a precise callback answer can recover.
- Untyped join over ProtocolDispatch's implementations (+2,987 with lr6): answers 'returns nothing' before an implementation lands, callers key on the guess and rebuild: shift wakes 2,859 -> 3,660, withdrawn activations 1 -> 35, InputDemand revisions 33 -> 297. Rejected.
- Join after every provider module is defined (+30,526, +8.4%): published once, shifts 2,247, but defines providers no receiver reaches (OptionParser fixtures +350..+600 each). Not proportional. Rejected.
Target: the callback's returned axis is joined over the implementations the receiver's type selects, as resolve_protocol_call already demands only overlapping providers (semantic.rs demand_overlapping_impl_providers). It needs demand stated per key, not per function, which is this ticket's policy.

Acceptance: panic/1 and fz_panic/1 are one activation each on the distiller; the suite passes on all three paths; every pin move is attributed and rises are authorized; type-specialization.md states the policy (callables, Ignore is not 'unread', specs do not key).

Landed (e53ea8074, draft PR #583 stacked on #580):
- Both key paths take the structural collapse; only a recursive key bounds it (callable -> address var, returned -> class). A non-recursive key keeps a callable's shape and a returned position verbatim. KeyCollapse::Literals is gone. Census -962 jobs, 0 fixtures up, withdrawals 1 -> 1; matrix green. Keeping the returned class (C2') was -1,372 but withdrew 10 more activations (non_empty_list normalised to list moves when demand becomes Whole).
- Item 1 answered: the 00420 mutually-subtype rise is new key arrows inheriting a closure's two alike-rendering ids; ceiling 122 -> 142 authorized, fz-sc8.203 tracks the collapse.
- Item 3 answered: keying still reads Recursive (it decides the bound), so its readers stay.
- Folded triple: World::activation_key_prerequisites.
- Acceptance panic/1: already met at base (no panic/1 or fz_panic/1 activation on the distiller, interp or build).
Not in this commit: item 2 (record class at unasked positions, B) and item 4 (per-receiver callback returned axis).
title: A key names what demand asks, in every body: the recursive/non-recursive keying split goes
